title: Developer Canary Sandbox: Playbook for Productized Canarying and Experimental Surface
author: Priya Patel
body:
Overview:

This playbook defines the Developer Canary Sandbox (DCS): a self-serve product surface that lets customers and internal teams run controlled canary experiments against Redwood inference surfaces (hosted, dedicated, and private) without impacting production SLAs or billing unpredictably. DCS combines a lightweight sandbox runtime, telemetry gates, cost controls, and an experiment orchestration UX targeted at engineering and platform teams.

Goals:
- Provide a safe, low-cost environment for customers to validate model variants, prompt changes, and routing/policy adjustments.
- Reduce time-to-confidence for canary releases from weeks to hours.
- Instrument experiments with the same telemetry provenance as production to provide valid signal for performance and quality decisions.
- Offer clear cost/crediting semantics so teams can run experiments without surprise bills.

Scope and audience:
- Primary audience: Developer/Platform engineers and Solutions Engineers running integration or fidelity experiments.
- Included: Hosted inference canaries (sandbox-hosted), Dedicated trial lanes (isolated capacity burst), Private lab (customer-managed lightweight sandbox package).
- Not included: Fully production traffic migrations, legal or compliance sign-offs (these require private deployment playbooks).

High-level product components:
1) Sandbox runtime image: tuned lightweight runtime with reduced resource limits, predictable latency floor, and configurable quantization profiles.
2) Experiment orchestration UI/CLI: create experiments, define traffic split, schedule rollouts, and attach evaluation sets.
3) Telemetry gating and provenance: automatically attaches experiment metadata to spans, sampling rules aligned to production telemetry, and an eval capture sink.
4) Cost & credit model: optional prepaid experiment credits, soft budget enforcement, and credit-escrow refund rules for no-op experiments.

Minimum Viable Product (MVP) requirements (must-haves):
- Experiment creation: name, target environment (hosted/dedicated/private), model variant, traffic percent, duration, and evaluation prompt set.
- Isolated quota bucket per experiment with a default 100k token soft limit.
- Telemetry tags: experiment_id, experiment_name, owner_team, model_variant, rollout_stage recorded on every request.
- Canary routing: support weighted routing (0.1% to 10%), immediate rollback API, and automatic safety cutoff if error rate > 5% for 5 consecutive minutes.
- Cost controls: per-experiment credit cap and opt-in prepaid credits.
- UX: a single-page experiment summary with status, telemetry sparkline (latency, error rate, cost burn), and quick rollback button.

Non-functional requirements:
- Sandbox SLOs: median token latency <= 1.5x production median for comparable configs; 95th perc latency spike detection enabled.
- Isolation: experiments cannot escalate to production compute pools.
- Telemetry fidelity: 95% of request-level telemetry fields must match production schema.
- Security: sandbox runs with reduced privileges; private sandboxes must still require KMS integration for tenant data.

Design considerations and trade-offs:
- Fidelity vs cost: DCS will support two fidelity tiers (high/low). High fidelity uses full tokenization/kv-cache paths; low fidelity uses reduced context and quantized kernels to reduce cost.
- Data capture: by default, experiment logs are ephemeral (30 days). Customers can opt into extended retention as a paid add‑on with legal review.
- Failure safety: prefer conservative safety cutoffs (error rate and latency) and automatic rollbacks. Complex heuristic-based rollback will be v1+.

Configuration table (recommended defaults):
| config_key | type | default | notes |
| experiment_token_cap | integer | 100000 | soft cap before auto-notify owner |
| safe_error_threshold_pct | decimal | 5.0 | sustained window = 5m |
| telemetry_sampling_pct | decimal | 50.0 | percent of requests forwarded to full trace sink |
| sandbox_fidelity | enum | low | options: low, high |
| retention_days | integer | 30 | optional paid longer retention |

Success metrics (measured during pilot):
- Median time from experiment creation to actionable result <= 4 hours.
- 90% of internal platform/solutions experiments avoid production incidents attributable to canary traffic.
- Customer satisfaction NPS > 8 for the sandbox onboarding flow.
- Average cost per experiment < $250 (benchmarked on median 10k tokens).

Telemetry and evaluation integration:
- Experiment metadata must be included in three sinks: ingestion metrics, tracing, and eval capture.
- Evaluation harness: attach a prompt-set that runs in shadow mode for every experimented request (optional), with aggregated quality deltas surfaced in the experiment UI.
- Alerts: prebuilt dashboards per experiment and rollout stage; automatic anomaly detection for latency and quality regressions.

Roadmap and milestones (high-level):
1) Q4 2026 (pilot): internal pilot with Solutions and 5 select customers; implement core routing and safety cutoffs.
2) Q1 2027 (self-serve beta): open self-serve onboarding, prepaid credits, and basic evaluation integration.
3) Q2 2027 (tiered fidelity + billing): add high-fidelity sandboxes and production-grade billing flows.
4) Q3 2027 (private sandboxes): ship customer-installable package for Private deployments with KMS/HSM integration.

Rollout checklist (step-by-step):
1. Internal validation: run 10 internal experiments across hosted and dedicated; confirm telemetry provenance and rollback behaviors.
2. Pilot customers onboarding: hand-hold first 5 customers; collect UX and billing feedback.
3. Automation hardening: add e2e tests for safety cutoff, quota enforcement, and telemetry mapping.
4. Open beta: enable self-serve sign-up and public docs.
5. Iterate on pricing packaging based on observed cost distribution and feedback.

Pricing and packaging notes (initial approach):
- Base model: prepaid experiment credits sold in micro-bundles (e.g., 10k-token blocks) with volume discounts.
- Add-on: extended telemetry retention and eval storage (monthly SKU).
- Dedicated trial lanes: sold as a time-bound reserved capacity SKU with a built-in credit allowance.
- Billing semantics: experiments consume tokens from the project/tenant; prepaid credits get debited first; overages bill at published sandbox rates (significantly discounted from production).

Release notes (first public beta):
- Feature set: experiment creation UI/CLI, weighted routing, telemetry gates, soft token caps, and instant rollback.
- Known limitations: no automated quality-based rollout (manual review required); private sandbox packaging in alpha.
- Migration notes: none for initial adopters, experiments are isolated and do not impact existing routes.

Open decisions and risks:
- Decision: default telemetry sampling rate (50%) vs cost — final rate requires pilot telemetry volume analysis.
- Risk: customers may treat sandbox results as production-equivalent; mitigation is clear product UX with fidelity badges and warnings.
- Decision: prepaid credit refund rules on experiment cancellation (recommended: prorated refund for unused tokens within 30 days).

Appendix: example CLI sequence to create a canary experiment:
1) Create an experiment via CLI:
   redwood dcs create --name "prompt-redesign-canary" --env hosted --model "rw-3b-v2" --percent 2 --duration 4h --tokens-cap 20000 --eval-set "prompt-redesign-v1"
2) Monitor status:
   redwood dcs status --id <experiment_id>
3) Rollback:
   redwood dcs rollback --id <experiment_id> --reason "latency spike"
